newsitem.title: USA: U.S. experts see Russia debt closing on track.
newsitem.headline: U.S. experts see Russia debt closing on track.

text.p: Emerging market experts expect Russia to close a roughly $35 billion debt restructuring by year-end despite the Thursday firing of security chief Alexander Lebed by President Boris Yeltsin.

"We see no reason to revise our expectation of a deal completion by the end of the year," said Thomas Trebat, managing director of emerging markets research at Citicorp Securities Inc, referring to Lebed's removal.
Completing the deal by year end is in the best interests of both the Russian government and its creditors, sources said.

"There is a lot of pressure to get the deal done before year-end from both sides because otherwise parts of it will need to be renegotiated," said Philip Poole, director of research for Eastern Europe and Russia at ING Barings in London. "My view is, yes, it is on track to close before year-end."
Russia's plan was to restructure approximately $35 billion of commercial debt known as Vneshekonombank loans, the borrowings of the former Soviet Union, and analysts say the deal was intact.

"I think we are still anticipating that today's political developments do not affect longer term financial issues in Russia, which are in Russia's long-term interest and its creditors' long-term interest," added Trebat.
Although Russia's Vnesh loans have widened out over the last two days, sources noted a trend in recent months in which risk of the deal's completion has diminished substantially.
"I think the deal risk, which is built into the prices of Vnesh loans, has not widened," said Trebat.

He explained that the deal risk "widened a little bit (Thursday) from where it had been but the long-term trend has been for that deal risk to decline very steadily over the summer months and, in the last couple of weeks, especially since the S&P and Moody's actions last week." he added.

On October 7, Standard and Poor's Corp assigned Russia a BB-minus rating on its foreign currency debt and Moody's Investors Service Inc assigned a prospective Ba2 sovereign ceiling on its foreign currency debt.
Earlier today, both agencies said that the removal of Lebed would not affect their current rating decisions.
Vneshekonombank loans fell sharply immediately after the announcement, but the debt recouped most of its losses but prices still remained down the recent highs.

Vnesh dollar loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were off one percentage point at 75-7/8 after falling as much as 2-1/2 earlier, and Vnesh Swiss franc denominated paper RUVNCHLNS=RR were down 1-1/8 after slipping as much as 73-1/8 bid.
Poole attributed the price drop over the last couple of days on concerns about Lebed and about potential problems with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
"It is not surprising that we have seen a correction to some extent or concern because this market has traded on political risk consistently and political risk has not gone away," Poole said.
